## Osthoff's posting to Turkey is cancelled

**Sources on this page:** p138 A1, p138 A2.

**Related source pages:** [p148 C1](148.md#source-p148-c1), [p149 A2](149.md#source-p149-a2).

<a id="edition-cases-people-osthoff-osthoffs-posting-to-turkey-is-cancelled"></a>


[Source audit](../../experiments/corpus_attack/SOURCE_FAMILIES.md)

Four receptions, p138 A1–A2 and p148 C1 / p149 A2, reconstruct the cancellation of Osthoff's posting to Turkey. Under the published **Nov4–6** key, they jointly support all **121 positions** of the first part and **115 of 118** in the second; three word repairs complete the proposed reading.

<a id="edition-cases-people-osthoff-most-likely-reading"></a>

### Most likely reading

**Readable German:**

> Militärmission Konstantinopel. Kommando des Hptms. der Res. Osthoff nach der Türkei und seine Zuteilung zur Militärmission ist aufgehoben. Derselbe ist dem 1. Ers. Batl. Eisenbahn-Regmts. zu überweisen. AKO folgt. Auf Allerhöchsten Befehl: Chef Militärkabinetts, Frhr. Marschall.

**English meaning:** To the Military Mission in Constantinople. Captain of the Reserve Osthoff's posting to Turkey and assignment to the Military Mission have been cancelled. He is to be transferred to the first replacement battalion of the railway regiment. The cabinet order will follow. By supreme command: the Chief of the Military Cabinet, Baron Marschall.

The English expands the military abbreviations *Ers. Batl.* and *AKO*. The cancellation concerns Osthoff's assignment. His full identity and the regiment number remain unestablished.

<a id="edition-cases-people-osthoff-what-the-witnesses-establish"></a>

### What the witnesses establish

| Part | Printed witnesses | Direct source evidence | Remaining editorial work |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | [p138 A1](../../experiments/corpus_attack/sources/childs_p138_A.png), [p148 C1](../../experiments/corpus_attack/sources/childs_p148_C1.png) | p148 fixes 120/121 positions. The other witness supplies the missing `R` in `DERRES`. All 121 candidate positions have complete coordinate-pair support in a witness. | The earlier p138 copy is five coordinates short. A unique best alignment among all 238 insertion positions supplies `XVAXX` before received index 140. Three other known-coordinate disagreements remain. |
| 2 | [p138 A2](../../experiments/corpus_attack/sources/childs_p138_A.png), [p149 A2](../../experiments/corpus_attack/sources/childs_p149_A2.png) | The two copies jointly support 115/118 proposed positions. p149 independently supplies the `N` in `KABINETTS` and the `C` in `HOECHSTEN`. | Both copies contain `UEM`, `ERSBKTL` and `REGM1S`. Reading `DEM`, `ERSBATL` and `REGMTS` requires three changes in p149 and four in the more damaged p138 copy. |

The literal p149 second part is:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
DERSELBEISTUEM1XERSBKTLEISENBAHNREGM1SZUUEBERWEISENAKOFOLGTXAUFALLERHOECHSTENBEFEHLCHEFMILITAERKABINETTSFRHRMARSCHALLX
```

</details>

Two repairs form the adjacent coordinate exchange `VF → FV` at transmitted indices 210–211; the third changes index 31 from `A` to `X`. The [certificate](../../experiments/corpus_attack/source_pair_results.json) records the raw readings, source differences, coordinate maps and repair costs.

<a id="edition-cases-people-osthoff-dates-and-provenance"></a>

### Dates and provenance

The p138 header gives 5 November; the clearer pp148–149 transmission was intercepted on 7 November and includes `0015 (6/11)`. Both parts use the unchanged published **Nov4–6** key. The later interception time therefore does not by itself require a new period key.

The historical records are from J. Rives Childs, *General Solution of the ADFGVX Cipher System*, printed pp138, 148–149 in the [source scan](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1_JiNMck7eUvdrOTrH7fsj1Yh44t-VSC6/view). The period-key work is credited to **George Lasry, Ingo Niebel, Nils Kopal and Arno Wacker**, with the public key also given by George Lasry in the [2017 discussion](https://scienceblogs.de/klausis-krypto-kolumne/2017/02/23/the-top-50-unsolved-encrypted-messages-46-unsolved-adfgvx-cryptograms-from-world-war-1/?all=1).

Source comparison, reconstruction and edition: **icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro**.

<a id="edition-cases-people-osthoff-reproduce"></a>

### Reproduce

```sh
python3 experiments/corpus_attack/build_source_pairs.py --verify
python3 experiments/corpus_attack/verify_source_pairs.py
```

The second implementation independently reconstructs the columns, checks all 238 missing-group positions and re-encrypts the candidate readings. The [full source audit](../../experiments/corpus_attack/SOURCE_FAMILIES.md) retains the exact raw texts and unresolved source disagreements.

## p138 B — Instruction to decipher first half from front and second half from back; likely 1410(5) reference to p132 B

**Edition context:** “First half from the front, second half from the back”.

<a id="edition-cases-radio-opposite-end-deciphering-first-half-from-the-front-second-half-from-the-back"></a>



**Source edition and verification: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.**

Childs p138 B gives a short operational instruction:

**Readable German — under the conditional final-X exclusion and stated word repairs:**

> Erste Hälfte von vorne, zweite Hälfte von hinten lösen. NKJ.

Its meaning is to solve or decipher the first half from the front and the
second half from the back. **The instructional body is shared by two equally
priced source variants.** The internal closing is `NKJ` in the preferred
variant and `NMJ` in the retained alternative. The separately printed
`NKJ 472` footer favors the former, without proving a unique geometry.

The edition is conditional: the source really contains **105 slots**, but
its readable body uses a 104-coordinate transposition with one extraneous
received coordinate separately retained. Two known-coordinate substitutions
and one invalid-glyph fill are also required. This is not an unchanged
ordinary-frame decryption.

<a id="edition-cases-radio-opposite-end-deciphering-exact-source-and-dates"></a>

### Exact source and dates

The primary source is J. Rives Childs, *General Solution of the ADFGVX Cipher
System*, [printed p138, PDF page 141](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1_JiNMck7eUvdrOTrH7fsj1Yh44t-VSC6/view).
The [full page](../../experiments/bidirectional_deciphering/sources/childs_p138_full.png)
is headed **6 November**, but the [B reception line](../../experiments/bidirectional_deciphering/sources/childs_p138_B.png)
reads **00.15 5 November**:

<details>
<summary>Literal source transcription</summary>

**Source transcription — clear header and/or literal source record:**

```text
B) LP v NKJ (00.15 November 5th)
SSD ZU 14.10 (5)
RICHI-105
NKJ 472
```

</details>

The `TEILE`/`RICHI` labels are overprinted, and the original image is retained.
The date contradiction is not silently repaired. There are 21 complete
five-character cipher groups; the fourth glyph of group 2, `FAARG`, is a
printed `R` outside the ADFGVX alphabet. It remains an erasure in analysis.
The external `NKJ 472` footer is outside the 105-slot ciphertext.

<a id="edition-cases-radio-opposite-end-deciphering-raw-readings-and-two-surviving-variants"></a>

### Raw readings and two surviving variants

Using all 105 slots in the unchanged published `Nov4-6` transposition gives
52 paired labels plus an unpaired `G`, and no readable body:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output — original odd frame; paired prefix is unreadable and an orphan coordinate remains:**

```text
EIM1VLM3LFT1VRF91R4KF19LW?HMYL4W9S3ML6NMJML1REELLTM2
```

</details>

Under the preferred conditional model, the **final received `X`, source
index 104**, is extraneous to a 104-coordinate cipher. Removing it for
transposition, while preserving it in the source witness, gives 51 fixed
labels out of 52:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output — conditional exclusion of final source 104 X:**

```text
ERSTEHAELFTEVONVORNEFFEIT?HAELFTEVONHINTENLOESENXNKJ
```

</details>

The proposal is:

<details>
<summary>Proposed text and exact labels</summary>

**Edited output — same conditional final-X exclusion, with the stated repairs:**

```text
ERSTEHAELFTEVONVORNEZWEITEHAELFTEVONHINTENLOESENXNKJ
```

</details>

Removing the preceding received **`F`, source index 103**, instead gives:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output — alternate conditional exclusion of source 103 F:**

```text
ERSTEHAELFTEVONVORNEFFEIT?HAELFTEVONHINTENLOESENXNMJ
```

</details>

After the same repairs, its complete alternative is:

<details>
<summary>Proposed text and exact labels</summary>

**Edited output — same alternate exclusion, with the stated repairs:**

```text
ERSTEHAELFTEVONVORNEZWEITEHAELFTEVONHINTENLOESENXNMJ
```

</details>

Both variants require exactly the same source edits:

| Source index, zero-based | Printed group / position, one-based | Change | Cost category |
| ---: | --- | --- | --- |
| 8 | 2 / 4 | printed `R` → `F` | One invalid-glyph fill |
| 76 | 16 / 2 | `V` → `F` | One known-coordinate substitution |
| 94 | 19 / 5 | `A` → `F` | One known-coordinate substitution |

The two substitutions restore `ZWEITE`; the fill supplies the missing `E`.
In addition, each variant separately charges **one extraneous transmitted
coordinate**, either the final `X` or the preceding `F`. Encoding either
52-character proposal, transposing at length 104, and reinserting its
unchanged extra coordinate produces **the same repaired 105-slot witness**.
Neither coordinate is silently deleted from the historical source.

The independently printed `NKJ 472` is evidence favoring the `NKJ` closing.
It is not part of the ciphertext or an additional coordinate repair. Calling
the final `X` intentional padding is a possible explanation, not an established
historical fact.

<a id="edition-cases-radio-opposite-end-deciphering-what-the-bounded-search-actually-found"></a>

### What the bounded search actually found

The archived comparison evaluated every single-coordinate insertion or
removal at two stages: before untransposition in the received stream, or
after untransposition in the intermediate stream. It supplied the one
published key, tried all six values of the printed `R` erasure and every
inserted coordinate, and used two unchanged frozen language objectives.

This completed **8,892 candidate records and 17,784 model-score evaluations**
over 422 geometric locations. The count includes repeated fill-value
witnesses; it is not a count of unique plaintexts. Both objectives tied the
two raw endings `NMJ` and `NKJ` at their highest score. The source footer,
rather than the scorer, favors the latter.

For the retrospective fixed `NKJ`-ending template, index 104 uniquely
minimizes substitutions among the 105 received-coordinate removal positions.
That statement is **conditional on the chosen closing**. Index 103 remains
equally cheap under its own `NMJ`-ending proposal. All original candidates,
ties and earlier unsuccessful stage interpretations remain in the
[phase archive](../../experiments/bidirectional_deciphering/search/original_phase_screen.json).

<a id="edition-cases-radio-opposite-end-deciphering-relation-to-p132-bs-1410-5-telegram"></a>

### Relation to p132 B's 1410 (5) telegram

The [p132 B source edition](132.md#edition-cases-radio-p132-radio-service-b-repeat-the-fourth-period-telegram-in-the-fifth)
contains this header:

<details>
<summary>Literal source transcription</summary>

**Source transcription — clear header and/or literal source record:**

```text
B) LP v NKJ (6.13 p.m., November 5th)
SSD EILT SOFORT LOESEN 1410 (5)
RIZI-155
```

</details>

The two records share the route **LP v NKJ**, the urgency label `SSD` and
the internal reference **1410 (5)**, with punctuation added in p138's
`ZU 14.10 (5)`. `ZU` explicitly introduces a reference to that time-stamped
message. These are concrete grounds for treating p138 as a likely related
instruction. They do not establish a reply in the reverse direction: the
printed route is the same in both. Nor is their chronological order fully
resolved, because p138's reception line and page heading conflict.

The preserved 622-block OCR-header inventory finds this time/day combination
only at p132 B and p138 B; another `1410` belongs to p177 with day `11/11`.
That is a bounded inventory of available OCR headers, not a universal
uniqueness claim about the original traffic.

<a id="edition-cases-radio-opposite-end-deciphering-a-precisely-limited-opposite-end-interpretation"></a>

#### A precisely limited opposite-end interpretation

The p132 source has 155 intermediate coordinates after its original
transposition is undone. With an odd length, pairing from the front and
pairing from the back use opposite pair phases. A finite comparison tried
all **78** ways to join an initial run of forward labels to a final run of
backward labels, leaving exactly one intermediate coordinate unpaired.

| Leading labels read from front | Trailing labels read from back | Unpaired intermediate index | Known-coordinate substitutions for the prior p132 proposal |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 27 | 50 | 54 | 3 |
| 28 | 49 | 56 | 3 |
| 38 | 39 | 76 | 20 |
| 39 | 38 | 78 | 22 |

The first two reproduce the earlier low-cost conditional p132 reading.
Their unpaired `V` belongs to the same run of four identical V coordinates
at indices **54–57** already retained in that edition. The literal balanced
halves, 38/39 or 39/38 labels, do **not** reproduce it at the same cost.

Thus the newly read instruction supports the general relevance of working
from opposite ends. A flexible split is algebraically the existing one-extra-
intermediate-coordinate model; it does not reduce that model's assumptions
or repair cost. The instruction does not explicitly identify intermediate
coordinates, a split point, or a mathematical procedure. **The p132 extra-V
interpretation remains conditional**, and none of these observations changes
the status of an unrelated challenge.

The two source models also act at different stages:

| Record | Conditional operation | Source-shaped forward witness |
| --- | --- | --- |
| p138 B | Exclude one received coordinate before 104-slot untransposition | Reinsert that same coordinate after transposition, preserving all 105 slots |
| p132 B | Exclude one intermediate V after 155-slot untransposition | Reinsert that V before transposition, preserving all 155 slots |

<a id="edition-cases-radio-opposite-end-deciphering-reproduce-and-attribution"></a>

### Reproduce and attribution

The [inputs](../../experiments/bidirectional_deciphering/inputs.json),
[certificate](../../experiments/bidirectional_deciphering/certificates.json)
and [method package](../../experiments/bidirectional_deciphering/README.md)
preserve all source bytes, image hashes, both full variants and the 78 finite
comparisons. The p132 inputs and certificate are frozen snapshots; its older
record is not modified by this comparison.

```sh
python experiments/bidirectional_deciphering/verify.py --verify
python experiments/bidirectional_deciphering/phase_audit.py --verify
```

The unchanged period key is prior work by **George Lasry, Ingo Niebel, Nils
Kopal and Arno Wacker**, [DOI 10.1080/01611194.2016.1169461](https://doi.org/10.1080/01611194.2016.1169461),
also published in George Lasry's [2017-02-24 comment 4](https://scienceblogs.de/klausis-krypto-kolumne/2017/02/23/the-top-50-unsolved-encrypted-messages-46-unsolved-adfgvx-cryptograms-from-world-war-1/?all=1).
Earlier unreviewed OCR and insertion-only candidates existed. No explicit
p138 B body example was found in the bounded author-paper review; no universal
first-decipherment priority is claimed.


<a id="edition-cases-radio-nov6-marine-service-notice"></a>

## p138 C — Marine-service notice: Heeresgruppe Kiew and Osmanie unavailable

**Edition context:** Osmanie unavailable: the 6 November marine-service notice.

<a id="edition-cases-radio-nov6-marine-service-notice-osmanie-unavailable-the-november-6-marine-service-notice"></a>



The telegram reports **Osmanie unavailable** and asks that all stations be
notified. Two source-mask fills complete the names **KIEW** and **OSMANIE**:
earlier telegrams independently supply both spellings from fully observed
coordinate pairs. Heeresgruppe Kiew appears among the recipients; the
literal address label **HZYU** has a separately priced **H. Qu.** proposal below.

<a id="source-p138-c"></a>
<a id="edition-cases-radio-nov6-marine-service-notice-completed-reading"></a>

### Completed reading

**Readable German — complete conditional reading with the two name fills:**

> Seekriegsleitung. Grosses HZYU. Admiral Berlin. Nachchef. Deutsche Marinevertr und Heeresgruppe Kiew. Osmanie ausgefallen. Alle Stellen benachrichtigen.

The reading has **143/143 fixed labels** in the existing conditional frame.
It requires **3 observed-coordinate substitutions, 6 source-mask fills and
1 added-slot fill**. The new name readings account for two of the source
fills and require no further change to an observed coordinate.

The frame treats a narrow stroke before `VAADA` as an extra mark and supplies
one coordinate at the end. These two assumptions remain necessary: the
native transcription and its different decoding are preserved below.

<details>
<summary>Completed stream and the two new mask values</summary>

**Edited output — completed conditional stream; 3 observed substitutions, 6 source-mask fills and 1 added-slot fill:**

```text
SEEKRIEGSLEITUNGGROSSESXHZYUXXADMIRALBERLINXXNACHCHEFXXDEUTSCHEXMARINEVERTRXUNDHEERESGRUPPEXKIEWXXOSMANIEAUSGEFALLENXALLESTELLENBENACHRICHTIGEN
```

All indices are zero-based and refer to the original 286-slot transcription.

| Field | Plaintext position | Native pair and domain | Added source fill | Independent name witness |
| --- | ---: | --- | --- | --- |
| `KIE?` → `KIEW` | 95 | `A?`: `17FHLW` | 44: printed `C` → `F` | [p110 B](110.md#edition-cases-military-kiew-morning-and-pioneer-reports-p110-b), raw `HRG KIEW` |
| `O?MANIE` → `OSMANIE` | 99 | `?G`: `23BHSV` | 146: printed `O` → `X` | [p77 B](077.md#edition-cases-context-radio-instructions-p77-b--call-sign-instruction-for-konia), raw `FUNKERABTLG OSMANIE` |

The witnesses use different period keys. Their complete name pairs are
recomputed in the [certificate](../../experiments/nov6_marine_service_notice/certificates.json);
they support these contextual selections from the native domains. Neither
source is a repeated copy of this notice.

</details>

The abbreviations `Nachchef` and `Marinevertr` are retained. The notice gives
no cause or duration for Osmanie's reported unavailability.

</details>

<a id="edition-cases-radio-nov6-marine-service-notice-optional-headquarters-address"></a>

### Optional headquarters address

The address may read **Grosses H. Qu.** (Grosses Hauptquartier). Independent raw telegrams use `HXQU`; applying that abbreviation here changes `GROSSESXHZYUXX` to `GROSSESXHXQUXX`.

The [p102 B1 Orient report](102.md#edition-cases-military-orient-south-slav-reports-p102-b1)
contains raw `GD X H X QU`; the [p86 A machine-gun enquiry](086.md#edition-cases-military-mg08-inventory)
contains raw `GR X H X QU`. Both abbreviation spans are entirely observed
under earlier period keys. They show usage of the abbreviation, not another
copy of this notice.

| Proposed label change | Pair change | Additional observed substitution |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Position 25: `Z` → separator `X` | `FV` → `FD` | Source 104: `V` → `D` |
| Position 26: `Y` → `Q` | `GV` → `GF` | Source 121: `V` → `F` |

Both printed `V` values are clear observations. This interpretation therefore
costs **two further substitutions**, bringing the complete conditional reading
to **5 observed substitutions, 6 source-mask fills and 1 added-slot fill**.
It supplies a plausible recipient without adding fixed positions: the cheaper
143-label layer above still reads `HZYU`. The original frame alternatives and
all numeric labels are unchanged.

<a id="edition-cases-radio-nov6-marine-service-notice-separate-frame-and-coordinate-costs"></a>

### Separate frame and coordinate costs

The two new name fills extend the earlier word layer; all other costs are
unchanged. No observed coordinate is excluded or reordered.

| Operation | Source position | Result |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| Exclude ambiguous masked mark | 225 | Omitted only in the conditional model |
| Add unknown slot | Boundary 286 | Added model slot 285, filled with `V` |
| Observed-coordinate substitution | 13 `A`→`F` | `E` in `AUSGEFALLEN` |
| Observed-coordinate substitution | 98 `V`→`F` | `E` in `STELLEN` |
| Observed-coordinate substitution | 174 `D`→`X` | `N` in `NACHCHEF` |
| Invalid `W` fill | 18 `W`→`V` | `G` in `GROSSES` |
| Invalid `W` fill | 84 `W`→`V` | `R` in `SEEKRIEGSLEITUNG` |
| Invalid `W` fill | 110 `W`→`V` | `U` in `UND` |
| Invalid `O` fill | 135 `O`→`X` | `I` in `SEEKRIEGSLEITUNG` |
| Invalid `C` fill, new | 44 `C`→`F` | `W` in `KIEW` |
| Invalid `O` fill, new | 146 `O`→`X` | `S` in `OSMANIE` |

<a id="edition-cases-radio-nov6-marine-service-notice-what-the-gap-comparison-establishes"></a>

### What the gap comparison establishes

After the stroke exclusion, the retained stream has 285 slots. The original
comparison prices all 286 single-gap alignments against the earlier partial
candidate, with its two unresolved names unconstrained. Adding the slot at
the end is the unique minimum in that family, at 3 observed substitutions.
The [certificate](../../experiments/nov6_marine_service_notice/certificates.json)
retains every price.

| Gap boundary in retained 285-slot stream | Observed substitutions |
| ---: | ---: |
| 280 | 6 |
| 281 | 5 |
| 282 | 4 |
| 283 | 4 |
| 284 | 4 |
| 285, at the end | 3 |

This comparison holds the stroke exclusion and selected body fixed. The
scan shows neither a cancellation through the stroke nor a blank proving a
final omission; other error models and plaintexts remain outside the test.

<a id="edition-cases-radio-nov6-marine-service-notice-source-restoration-attribution-and-reproduction"></a>

### Source restoration, attribution and reproduction

Earlier OCR had 279 slots: it omitted the final `FVAAA`, the invalid `W`
after `VXVX`, and the narrow stroke. The [prior-work record](../../experiments/nov6_marine_service_notice/prior_candidates.json)
preserves that input and its unchanged-key output.

Source edition and verification: **icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro**. Childs
supplies the historical collection. The Nov4–6 period key retains the credit
of George Lasry, Ingo Niebel, Nils Kopal and Arno Wacker, with its published
provenance recorded in the inputs.

[Inputs](../../experiments/nov6_marine_service_notice/inputs.json),
[name-completion evidence](../../experiments/nov6_marine_service_notice/label_completion.json),
[certificates](../../experiments/nov6_marine_service_notice/certificates.json),
and [reproduction instructions](../../experiments/nov6_marine_service_notice/README.md)
preserve the native frame, source mapping, earlier word repairs, independent
name witnesses and complete re-encryption of the conditional reading.
